note: Independent first-principles predictions made blind to the size study's simulation (two analysts: scaling of the 60 cm body to 57 and 54 cm; catalog and packaging for larger drives at 75 and 80 cm). Kept to compare with the simulated results in SIZE_STUDY.md.

catalog_75_80cm.overall_answer:
Short answer: yes. The 75 cm body can take larger drives at the hips and neck now, on 24 V and without widening the hips. An 80 cm body is not needed for that, and it would not help: it raises the loads by about 6–15 % and adds only about 7 % of room.

**(a) Requirements and qualifying parts.** I took each worst case from the sizing records, the Froude 0.05 walk (1.25 × peak, 1.15 × speed) and the turning verdicts, and required each to be at most 0.80 of the part's limit.
- **Hip roll and thigh twist:** the MyActuator X4-36-L qualifies on both buses (0.70–0.74). The CubeMars AK45-36 sits at 0.93–0.97.
- **Neck:** only the ROBOTIS XM540-W270 servo qualifies (0.67). It has the same box, mass and price as the W150.
- **Tail:** the Tapered body needs the Feetech STS3250 (Froude 0.05 peak 0.87 → 0.52). The Hybrid body keeps its STS3215 (0.77).
- **Ankles:** they keep the X4-36-L (0.70–0.71).
- **Hip pitch:** no part qualifies on 24 V once the Froude 0.05 speed counts. The closest are the CubeMars AK10-9 (sustained 0.82/0.87) and the MyActuator X6-60 (speed 0.83/0.82). On 48 V the RobStride 03 itself qualifies (sustained 0.74/0.78, speed 0.54), and X6-60, RobStride 04, X8 and X12 also do.
- **Knee:** the Froude 0.05 walk needs 8.2–8.4 rad/s with margin. The X4-36-L gives 8.69 rad/s on either bus, because the rules give no speed credit above its 24 V rating. No 55 mm part qualifies. The lightest-cheapest that does is the 88 mm RobStride 06 (0.54–0.58); the others are 89–98 mm CubeMars parts.

**Case (i): 20 % headroom applied to the sizing walks only.** The bus stays 24 V with the 6S 3300 pack.
- Parts: X4-36-L hip roll and twist, X6-60 hip pitch, XM540-W270 neck; everything else unchanged.
- This is the earlier Froude 0.05 what-if body plus the X4-36-L hip roll and the W270 neck.
- Hip spacing goes from 187.0 to 198.5 mm.
- Result: 14.58 / 14.70 kg (−0.32 kg), $18.37k / $18.42k nominal (+$1.0k), 37.6 / 37.3 min (−0.6 min).
- Margins stay thin: thigh twist 0.78, Hybrid hip pitch 0.77, knee speed 0.76.
- At Froude 0.05 the body passes the 1.0 limits but not 0.80: hip pitch 0.83, knee 0.95–0.97.

**Case (ii): 20 % headroom including the Froude 0.05 walk.**
- **Bus:** 24 V is infeasible, so it goes to 48 V. That brings a pack twice as heavy (two 6S 3300 in series: +0.65 kg with its cassette, double the energy) and the 48 V power bay (+0.32 kg).
- **Knees:** they become RobStride 06 (+0.26 kg each).
- **First pass:** X4-36-L roll and twist, RobStride 03 hip pitch (its hold falls 1–3 %, because the pack sits behind the hip), RobStride 06 knees.
- **The weak point:** the extra pack mass behind the hip and the heavier swing legs push the thigh-twist hold to about 5.0–5.3 N·m. That is 0.84–0.88 of the X4-36-L, over 0.80; I put this at about 70–75 % likely.
- **The cascade:** the catalog has nothing between the 55 mm X4-36-L and the 79–80 mm parts, so the twist and then the hip roll step to the CubeMars AK60-39. Those are the 100 cm class's parts, and they set the hips at about 233 mm.
- **Most likely result:** about 19.0 / 19.1 kg (+4.1 kg), about $20.0k (+$2.6k), about 64–65 min.
- **If the X4-36-L twist holds:** 16.9 / 17.0 kg, $18.56k / $18.55k, about 64 min, hips unchanged at 187 mm.
- On the Hybrid body the RobStride 03 hip pitch stays near 0.78; if it tips over 0.80 it becomes a RobStride 04 (about +1.2 kg).

**(b) What sets the hip spacing.** In the tandem layout the half-spacing is: (hip-roll diameter / 2 + 6.5 mm) + 4 mm + (the larger of hip-pitch length and thigh-twist diameter, / 2 + 7.5 mm) + 0.02 B + 4.4 mm for the pelvis plate. That gives 187.0 mm now.
- The RobStride 03's 62 mm installed length governs over the twist's 60 mm diameter.
- So the X4-36-L for roll and twist, and the RobStride 03 or 04 for hip pitch, leave the spacing unchanged.
- The X6-60 hip pitch adds 11.5 mm. AK60-39 twist and roll add 11 and 12 mm per side.
- The packaging score term is small (2.6 g of score per mm at 16 kg). The 24 mm step to 84 mm costs 0.064 kg of score against 0.39 kg of real mass, so the term does not prevent the cascade.

**(c) Fit.**
- **Hip parts fit.** The X4-36-L has the same 60 mm installed diameter and is 4.5 mm longer; the rear roll motor still leaves 3.9–5.9 mm before the tail pivot. A RobStride 04 (125 mm installed) fits inside the 84.6 / 96.1 mm upper-thigh fairing radius, which it needs 74.5 mm of.
- **Neck and tail servos fit.** Each upgrade has the same box as the part it replaces.
- **The knee drive does not fit.** The generator puts the 88 mm RobStride 06 at 0.84 of the 215 mm femur. Its envelope then covers the knee axis by 12.6 mm (18.6 mm with the AK60-39 twist). Today's knee drive clears the axis by 24.9 mm, and the 100 cm class's 106 mm knee clears its axis by about 40 mm on a 287 mm femur.
- **The 233 mm hips** match the 60 cm body's proportion (0.46 H) and the 100 cm class's absolute width, but they need re-screening.

**(e) 80 cm (scale 1.067).** With the same parts:
- Loads: mass +5–6 %, hip-pitch hold +13–15 % (about 9.5 / 10.1 N·m), roll +4–6 %, twist +6–8 %, knee and ankle +10–12 %, neck +15–20 %.
- Froude-scaled joint speeds fall only 3.2 %.
- Room: the hips are set by the hardware (+1.4 mm), the femur grows 14 mm and the thigh fairing about 6 mm.
- The 75 cm round-two parts would then exceed even the 1.0 limits: twist 1.02–1.04, neck servo about 1.13, hip-pitch Froude 0.05 speed about 1.05.
- The extra 14 mm of femur is just enough for the 88 mm knee drive to clear the knee axis (+1.7 mm). But the 80 cm hip pitch needs the RobStride 04, whose larger diameter takes that back (−5.3 mm).
- Predicted results: about 19 kg on 24 V (brisk-only headroom: RobStride 04 or X8-150 hip pitch, AK60-39 roll and twist), or about 21 kg on 48 V with Froude 0.05 headroom, at $20–21k.
- So 80 cm raises the requirements more than it makes room.

This is a prediction from record sensitivities, the build and sizing formulas, and a simple lever model of the holds. I built and sized no models. The scripts are /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-mesozoic-labs/c17e65d8-8171-548a-aef1-2a557e9379dd/scratchpad/r2/sizepred/req_table.py and /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-mesozoic-labs/c17e65d8-8171-548a-aef1-2a557e9379dd/scratchpad/r2/sizepred/geom.py. The 60 cm "5–10 % smaller" question is not covered here.

risks_and_caveats: The main fork is the X4-36-L thigh twist on the 48 V body. I estimate 0.84-0.88 against a 0.80 limit, but a +/-0.04 error flips the outcome between about 17 kg with 187 mm hips (ii-A) and about 19 kg with 233 mm hips (ii-B). The hold model is a lever model calibrated to one point plus variant sensitivities (65-80 N·m per metre of half-spacing; about 1.4% per 1% of mass). It is not a solved hold.

The Hybrid hip pitch on the RobStride 03 sits at about 0.76-0.78 against 0.80. If it goes over, the RobStride 04 (+0.54 kg each, 120 mm) is next, adding about 1.2 kg and making the knee stack worse (knee station 0.90 at 75 cm).

Which case applies depends on the size study's exact rule: 20% on all groups, the per-group override the current sizing.py now supports, and whether the Froude 0.05 walk joins the sizing walks or is only screened. Case i and case ii differ by about 4 kg and 26 min of runtime.

The Tapered body may alternate between 24 V and 48 V: with the rear 12S pack the AK10-9 just passes on 24 V (about 0.797), and with the 6S pack it fails again. The current pipeline has a rule that then settles on the higher bus, so the record may carry an oscillation note.
The RobStride 06 has no sourced phase resistance; the power model uses the 0.25 ohm fallback and flags it. The +14 to +18 W knee power, and so the runtime, are uncertain.

The clearance screen excludes parent/child pairs, so the femur-mounted knee drive overlapping the knee axis and the shank's tibia plates may not be flagged by any gate. The 12.6 mm overlap is a geometry finding from the stacking rule, not a screen result. Building it would need the knee drive moved, which is a generator change.

The sizing speed requirement for the thigh twist ignores turning. An AK60-39 twist on 24 V would pass sizing but sit at 0.86-0.87 of its 3.67 rad/s in the 0.50 rad/s walking turn. This matters for the 80 cm 24 V cascade.

Mass growth of structure and covers (load-sized beams, the larger lower-thigh fairing, wider pelvis covers) is estimated at +0.1 to +0.4 kg. The cascade's spacing increase also raises roll and twist walk RMS, which I scaled by hand.

80 cm numbers use scaling exponents (M about s^0.85 at fixed parts; hip-pitch lever about s^1.2), not a built model. The forward-moment growth could be steeper, as round one's 60 to 75 cm exponent of 3.9 suggests, which would only strengthen the conclusion that 80 cm raises requirements.

Independence: I did not open round2/size_study/. git status listed its untracked subfolder names, and I saw the current sizing.py and pipeline.py rule code (per-group headroom, bus-oscillation handling) but no size-study results. The earlier committed Froude 0.05 what-if records (round2/whatif_fr05) were used as a calibration point.
This covers only the 75 / 80 cm question. The owner's other question (a 5-10% smaller 60 cm body) is not addressed here.

scaling_60cm_smaller.overall_answer:
Shrinking the 60 cm body by 5 or 10 % (crown 57 or 54 cm, same proportions, same parts) does not buy margin in the sense that matters. The torque-to-weight improvement is small. The ratio that actually limits the 60 cm design, the knee's speed, gets worse. And the packaging is already tight at 57 cm and fails at 54 cm.

Why:
1. Mass falls only 2.7 % (57 cm: T 10.56 kg, H 10.66 kg) and 5.3 % (54 cm: T 10.28 kg, H 10.36 kg). About 55 % of the robot is catalog hardware that does not scale (drives 4.16 kg, battery, power, compute, control, servos, sensors, fasteners). Most of the structure also scales only linearly: the plates are already at the 3 mm minimum, with widths set by the drives. Effective law: M ∝ H^0.52, not H^3.
2. The loads whose moment arms scale with height fall: ankle −8 / −15 %, neck −12 / −22 %, hip pitch −16 / −32 %. The hip-pitch drop is helped by the CoM moving aft relative to H, because the battery cassette and tail pivot stay fixed behind the hip. But the lateral hip loads are set by the hip and foot spacing, which the drive envelopes fix at 93.9 → 93.1 mm. So the hip roll falls only with mass (−2 / −4.5 %), the thigh twist hardly at all (3.52 → 3.47 → 3.43 N·m), and the knee hold stays flat (3.17 → 3.15 → 3.14).
3. In Froude-scaled walks the joint angular speeds rise like H^-1/2 (+2.6 % at 57, +5.4 % at 54; the knee measured +1.4 / +4.9 %).

Ratios with the 60 cm drives (T family; H is similar):
- Sizing walks: hip-yaw continuous 0.771 → 0.761 → 0.751; ankle 0.763 → 0.703 → 0.645; neck 0.761 → 0.673 → 0.592. The knee speed 0.771 → 0.782 → 0.809 becomes the governing group, so the worst ratio rises from 0.771 to 0.782 and 0.809 (H family: 0.786 → 0.797 → 0.808).
- Froude 0.05 walk: knee speed 0.960 → 0.972 → 1.015 (H: 0.983 → 0.994 → 1.006). The 54 cm body exceeds its knee drive in the animal-like walk.

Re-selection under the round-two rule picks the same six leg drives at both sizes. The catalog parts just below are either too weak (AK45-10 and X2-P28 at 1.43 N·m) or too slow (AK45-36 at 4.19 rad/s for the hip pitch and knee). The X4-P12 misses the 54 cm hip-pitch peak by 6 %, and the AK45-10 misses the ankle hold by 3 %. Only the neck servo could drop to the STS3215 at 54 cm, and only at 0.98-0.99 of its rating. Build cost falls 2.0 % (−$290) at 57 cm and 3.4 % (−$510) at 54 cm. With the 0.80 headroom option in sizing.py, the 54 cm knee would need a RobStride 06, which adds 0.52 kg.

Packaging:
- Knee drive: it stays 135 mm down the femur, so at 57 cm it reaches the knee axis and at 54 cm it intrudes 8 mm into the top of the shank. The clearance screen does not check femur–shank pairs, so it will not flag this.
- Knee flexion (thigh shell against calf): about 0.71 rad at 57 cm, which passes the 0.10 rad gate with 0.13 to spare. At 54 cm it is about 0.59 rad at ankle station 0.46 and about 0.65 rad at the search's maximum of 0.50, so it fails the gate.
- Camera: at 57 cm it fits with 7 mm of width margin. At 54 cm it fits with essentially none, sitting lower and further back.
- Tail pivot setback grows from 40 to 61 mm.

In short, 57 cm is feasible but gains nothing, and 54 cm is worse. Margin at 60 cm has to come from the knee drive's speed and the thigh-twist hold, not from a smaller body.

Method: I worked only from the committed round-two records and models; I did not open round2/size_study/. For the masses I applied each 60 cm ledger row's own generator rule. For the loads I scaled the recorded 60 cm MuJoCo model by s in x and z, kept the hardware-set lateral offsets and drive offsets, re-massed it from those rules, and ran the study's own statics, gait, turning, sizing.select and camera-search code on it. At s = 1 this reproduces every recorded 60 cm hold, requirement, Froude 0.05 screen and camera fit to 4 decimals.

risks_and_caveats: This is an emulation, not a generator rebuild. I placed hardware by hand from the build.py rules, and approximated the generator's hull widening and cover shapes with exponents (s^1.85 for trunk panels, s^2 for head/tail, partly fixed thigh/calf). Expect about ±0.1 kg on mass and a few percent on the holds.

Several verdicts sit within 1-2 % of a threshold and could flip in the full computation: the Froude 0.05 knee at 54 cm (1.015 T, 1.006 H; walk-generator noise is about 1 %), the neck downgrade to STS3215 at 54 cm (0.98-0.99 of its rating), the 0.80-headroom knee at 54 cm (0.808-0.809), and the X4-P12 hip-pitch peak shortfall at 54 cm (6 %).

The camera fit moves the 0.10 kg camera about 2-4 mm back and 2-5 mm down relative to my scaled head. I did not feed that into the neck torque. Its effect is about 1 % of the 54 cm neck load, which slightly favours the STS3215.

The knee-flexion estimate comes from translating the 60 cm convex proxies; the shell shapes were not regenerated. The s = 1 sweep gives 0.80 rad against the screen's 0.811, so I quoted deltas. Uncertainty is about ±0.03 rad, and the 54 cm verdict at station 0.50 (margin about 0.09 vs the 0.10 gate) is inside it.

The knee-drive overlap with the shank top at 54 cm is a geometric fact of the thigh-pod stack rule. The study's clearance screen will not report it, because femur–shank (parent–child) pairs are excluded.
If the sizing loop dropped the neck to the STS3215 at 54 cm, the session-heat screen would put the neck at about 0.99 of its sustained torque, making it the hottest drive.

Scaled items' central inertias were scaled as (m_s/m_60)·s²; catalog parts kept their own. This affects only the walk inertial terms, and the gravity-dominated holds match the scaling laws within 2 %.

Re-selection used the round-two rule (HEADROOM 1.0, 24 V tried first). The 0.80 headroom result is my reading of the option in sizing.py; I do not know whether the size study applies it to the 54/57 cm cases.
The owner's 75 cm larger-motor / 80 cm question is outside this step; I did not address it.
